newsitem.title: FRANCE: France could delay Fr.Telecom sale.
newsitem.headline: France could delay Fr.Telecom sale.

text.p: The French government is considering delaying the sale of a stake in telecommunications group France Telecom SA due to the early parliamentary election in May and June, an official source said on Tuesday.

Under the original timetable, the state would have announced the price range for the sale on May 5 and the final price on the evening of May 26. President Jacques Chirac announced the snap election on Monday and the first round of the poll will be on May 25.
The sale of a 30 percent stake in France Telecom, valued at between 160 and 210 billion francs, would be the biggest market operation in the country.
Financial analysts had said that the snap election would increase the political risks of the sale.

"It all depends on the French share market. If the market falls 10 percent due to the political situation they will have to look at the valuation again but if the market stays flat it could still go ahead as planned," said analyst Robert Mocatta at BZW in London.

"The market does not like additional risk. It looks like (Prime Minister Alain) Juppe stands to win again but with a smaller majority. I see no reason to change my France Telecom valuation," another analyst said.
At France Telecom there was no comment on the report. "I have no comment whatsoever at the moment. I wait," a spokesman said.
At the Prime Minister's office and at the Finance Ministry there was no immediate official comment.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told Europe 1 radio on Monday that planned privatisations would go ahead.
"All that has been launched will be carried out according to schedule," he said.
Industry Minister Franck Borotra said on Sunday, also to Europe 1, that an early election would not affect the timetable of France Telecom's Initial Public offering (IPO).
"Today, the question is to know at what actual level the public offering will take place," he said.
Other outstanding state asset sale operations are the privatisation of defence electronics group Thomson-CSF and the sale of further shares in computer maker Cie des Machines Bull.

Alcatel Alsthom and Dassault Industrie cancelled a news conference today at which they would have outlined what they planned to do with Thomson-CSF. Lagardere Groupe is another biddder. The two final bids have to be presented to the government before May 7.
For Bull, the sale price is scheduled to be announced on Tuesday evening.
